lens: Interaction and responsive accessibility. Visual review of all fourteen account crops and the motivating screenshot only. No implementation inspection or interaction testing. Scores do not establish keyboard support, semantics, hit-area dimensions, or measured contrast compliance. Account crops show Claude; Codex styling is not assessed.

findings: Before — hierarchy 7, layout 7, content 7: closed rows expose Pro/100 pts, Current, and multiple limit values. Move ordinary plan and limit details into expansion; retain name, balance, and warning summaries.

Before — colour 8, responsive/accessibility 8: cloud credits at 0% and the five-hour limit at 14% communicate their warning status through yellow numerals alone. Add concise textual warning cues beside these values.
Before — controls/states 8: the tiny, dim leading chevrons provide weak visual disclosure cues. Increase their visible size and contrast without increasing row bulk.

After — content falls 7 to 6: account 1's yellow 0% cloud-credit warning and account 2's yellow 14% five-hour warning disappear while both rows show 82.8%. Retain a short warning summary identifying the affected limit in each closed row.
After — colour 8, responsive/accessibility 8: restore the missing warning summaries with both amber emphasis and explicit text; the white overall balances currently provide no visible warning cue.
After — controls/states falls 8 to 7: Expand All loses its outlined button treatment and resembles adjacent metadata. Restore a restrained boundary or background and strengthen the row chevrons.
After — consistency falls 9 to 8: Expand All is plain text here but remains outlined in the narrow screenshots. Use the same recognizable control treatment across widths.
Positive: the crop decreases from 171 to 74 pixels high, with names and balances cleanly aligned.

Before — hierarchy 7, layout 7, content 7: the two-column limit grids make closed accounts several lines tall. Move normal limits, plan details, and Current into expansion while keeping warning summaries visible.
Before — colour 8, responsive/accessibility 8: the yellow 0% cloud-credit value and 14% five-hour value lack textual warning qualifiers. Add short labels identifying exhausted or low limits.
Before — controls/states 8: small, dim row chevrons are easy to overlook beside the bold balances. Increase their visible size and contrast.
After — content falls 7 to 6: removing the limit grids also removes account 1's 0% and account 2's 14% warnings. Preserve concise limit-specific warnings beneath or beside the corresponding names.
After — colour 8, responsive/accessibility 8: both affected accounts now appear unqualified at 82.8%. Use text plus amber emphasis for the retained warning summaries.
After — controls/states falls 8 to 7: Expand All becomes unbounded text. Restore a compact button treatment and clearer row disclosure indicators.
After — consistency falls 9 to 8: desktop Expand All loses the outline retained at narrow widths. Keep its visual treatment consistent.
Positive: the crop decreases from 226 to 74 pixels high without visible name or balance clipping.
Before — hierarchy 7, layout 6, content 7: closed accounts stack full limit grids and occupy 587 pixels. Hide ordinary plan and limit details until expansion, retaining compact warning summaries.

Before and after — typography/numbers 8: the header strands eligible on a second line and splits Expand All across two lines. Place account counts on their own header line and keep the action label together.
Before — colour 8: the 0% cloud-credit and 14% five-hour warnings rely on yellow numerals. Add explicit warning text.
Before and after — controls/states 8: the leading disclosure chevrons remain tiny and dim. Make them more legible while preserving the compact row spacing.
Before — responsive/accessibility 7: the wrapped header and colour-only warning status hinder scanning. Reflow the header and label the warnings in text.
After — content falls 7 to 6: account 1's 0% warning and account 2's 14% warning are hidden behind identical 82.8% summaries. Keep short limit-specific warning text in the closed rows.
After — colour 8, responsive/accessibility 8: restore amber warning summaries with text, and reflow the cramped header without shrinking its lettering.

Before — hierarchy 7, layout 6, content 7: a three-line credential name is followed by plan text, Current, and a full limit grid. Move ordinary details into expansion and retain only name, balance, and warnings when closed.
